newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Occidental shuns Vietnam venture - report.
newsitem.headline: Occidental shuns Vietnam venture - report.

text.p: Occidental Chemical Corp., a unit of Los Angeles-based Occidental Petroleum Corp. of the United States, has pulled out of a $109 million polyvinyl-chloride (PVC) resin venture in southern Vietnam, the Vietnam Investment Review said on Sunday.
The state-controlled weekly said Occidental Chemical walked away from the venture with Marubeni Corp. and two local firms because the authorities had licensed a rival project.

"When we entered into it, we had the understanding that there was just going to be one licensee," the magazine quoted Occidental Petroleum's public affairs vice president in Texas, Charles Dana, as saying.
"When we found out there were going to be two, that changed the whole picture," he said.

The venture, Oxy-vina Plastics and Chemical Co. Ltd., was to be 40 percent owned by Occidental Chemical, 30 percent by Marubeni and 15 percent by each of the two Vietnamese firms, Vietnam Gas Co. and Import-Export-Technical Raw Material Trading and Supply Co. The venture's plant was to have been located at Phu My, near Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon.
The authorities subsequently licensed another PVC resin plant, a $90 million venture also close to Ho Chi Minh City.
